Common pitfalls

What to avoid

  • Using fixed chunk sizes without considering document structure.
  • Not measuring retrieval quality separately from generation quality.
  • Stuffing too much context into the prompt, exceeding useful context window usage.

Build an end-to-end RAG pipeline

advanced coding

Implement a complete RAG pipeline: document chunking, embedding, retrieval, context assembly, and prompt construction. Use mock embeddings for testing.

What to notice

  • Cosine similarity for retrieval: dot / (norm * norm)
  • Prompt should clearly separate context from the question

Reference solution 
import numpy as np
from typing import List

def embed(text: str) -> np.ndarray:
    np.random.seed(hash(text) % 2**32)
    return np.random.randn(64)

class RAGPipeline:
    def __init__(self):
        self.chunks = []
        self.embeddings = []

    def ingest(self, document: str, chunk_size: int = 200, overlap: int = 50):
        words = document.split()
        for i in range(0, len(words), chunk_size - overlap):
            chunk = ' '.join(words[i:i + chunk_size])
            if chunk:
                self.chunks.append(chunk)
                self.embeddings.append(embed(chunk))

    def retrieve(self, query: str, top_k: int = 3) -> List[str]:
        query_emb = embed(query)
        scores = []
        for i, emb in enumerate(self.embeddings):
            sim = np.dot(query_emb, emb) / (np.linalg.norm(query_emb) * np.linalg.norm(emb))
            scores.append((sim, i))
        scores.sort(reverse=True)
        return [self.chunks[i] for _, i in scores[:top_k]]

    def generate_prompt(self, query: str, context: List[str]) -> str:
        ctx = '\n---\n'.join(context)
        return f"""Answer the question based on the context below.\n\nContext:\n{ctx}\n\nQuestion: {query}\nAnswer:"""

Evaluate RAG retrieval quality

intermediate coding

Implement precision@k, recall@k, and MRR metrics for evaluating a retrieval system given ground truth relevant documents.

What to notice

  • P@k = (relevant in top-k) / k
  • R@k = (relevant in top-k) / total_relevant
  • MRR = 1/rank of first relevant document

Expected outcome

P@3: 0.333, R@3: 0.333, MRR: 0.500

Reference solution 
from typing import List

def precision_at_k(retrieved: List[str], relevant: List[str], k: int) -> float:
    top_k = retrieved[:k]
    relevant_set = set(relevant)
    return len([d for d in top_k if d in relevant_set]) / k

def recall_at_k(retrieved: List[str], relevant: List[str], k: int) -> float:
    top_k = retrieved[:k]
    relevant_set = set(relevant)
    return len([d for d in top_k if d in relevant_set]) / len(relevant_set)

def mrr(retrieved: List[str], relevant: List[str]) -> float:
    relevant_set = set(relevant)
    for i, doc in enumerate(retrieved):
        if doc in relevant_set:
            return 1.0 / (i + 1)
    return 0.0

Worked example

RAG for internal knowledge bases with mixed document types

A company has 50K internal documents (Confluence pages, PDFs, Slack threads, code docs) and wants employees to ask natural language questions.

Recommended choice

Build a multi-source ingestion pipeline with format-specific parsers, semantic chunking, and a unified vector index.

Why it fits

  • Different document types need specialized parsers (PDF layout, Slack threads, code structure).
  • Semantic chunking preserves meaning boundaries better than fixed-size splitting.
  • Metadata (author, date, team, document type) enables filtered retrieval for relevance.

If you chose differently

Treating all documents as plain text with fixed-size chunks loses structural information and mixes unrelated content in the same chunk.

Interview-ready takeaway

Quality RAG requires treating ingestion as seriously as generation. Most failures trace to poor chunking or missing metadata.
